items.note: Two-group experiment in which 64 design students did a three-hour cane design task with AIGC tools (ChatGPT, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion) or traditional software; rated creative performance higher with AIGC (d = 0.55), plus EEG; the abstract does not say how students were allocated (some search notes claim random assignment).

System paper (NexusAI) with a within-subject study (N = 14) comparing an LLM-inspiration diagramming tool to a baseline on design space exploration and fixation; the baseline is likely another AI interface, and N is below 50.

Quasi-experiment over four task rounds comparing a GenAI multi-agent system with a single-agent model for undergraduates' creative problem solving; outcome is creative thinking ability (possibly a test rather than scored output); abstract read from the publisher page via web search, APIs had none; N not stated.

Fashion pattern design experiment comparing AI style-transfer-extended designs with human-originated designs, assessed by expert evaluation, subjective ratings and eye-tracking; unclear whether participants worked under different AI conditions or whether it compares outputs only (could be context_ai_vs_human or out); N not stated.

Two online experiments comparing product ideas from humans, GPT-4, and human-GPT co-creation modes (human ideas revised with GPT) on quality and diversity (human and deep-learning evaluations); mixes an AI-vs-human comparison with participant co-creation arms; SSRN working paper, abstract from Crossref.

Comparative quasi-experiment with college design students using ChatGPT-4, DeepSeek, or conventional creative methods; outcomes are AI-assisted design performance, creative self-efficacy and engagement; N not stated.

Sixty university students randomly assigned to create digital stories over 20 weeks with GAI tools (ChatGPT, Midjourney, Runway) or traditional methods; team creativity performance higher with GAI, but the abstract says outcomes came from pre/post surveys and interviews, so the creativity measure may be self-reported.

Mixed-methods study in which 47 participants wrote analysis and synthesis texts with or without AI suggestions, measuring textual overlap between AI suggestions and final text, plus a think-aloud (n = 4) of a reflective interface; outcome is suggestion reuse, not creativity or cross-writer diversity, and N is below 50 (likely out at full text); FAccT 2026 and arXiv 2605.15322 are the same work.

Within-subjects study (N = 24) on a poster image creation task comparing the HAICo divergent/convergent co-creation system with ChatGPT (AI configuration comparison); creativity dimensions may be self-rated; N below 50.

Large field experiment on an online labor market in which employers were randomly offered AI-written first drafts of job posts; treated posts were more generic and less informative; the task is job-post writing, not a creative task, so scope is doubtful (genericness may be the only diversity-adjacent outcome); abstract from the author's page via web search, SSRN abstract not in APIs.
